decision: Did not close. The provider reports the job complete (event-039) and the request was marked completed without payment because the landlord pays the contractor directly (event-040, event-041), but two definition-of-done items remain open: landlord confirmation of completion, and verification that the originally reported fault — the basin cold tap "isn't working at all" (event-001) — is actually resolved, since the only evidence is the provider's second-hand account of what the tenants said. I asked the landlord to confirm completion and which firm to record (ACT-1), asked the tenant to confirm both the WC fill and the basin tap are right (ACT-2), referred the contradiction in our own records about the instructed provider to the office (ACT-3), logged the file note (ACT-4) and put the case on hold (ACT-5). No dispatch and no spend were made: no quote exists, no amount appears in the file, and no standing cap is on file.

facts.statement: Tenant reported on 2 Oct 2024 that the only WC fills by trickling and the bathroom basin cold tap does not work at all; the WC drains away normally and there are pets at the property.
Urgency is routine: no emergency definition is met — the WC drains, water supply and other taps are available, no hazard keyword and no vulnerability is disclosed anywhere in the file.
The agency raised and briefed a work order on 2 Oct and told the tenant a provider would attend.
The only landlord message in the visible history is 'Thanks Ava' (2 Oct), replying to the agency's note that a job had been raised; it names no amount.
No spend cap or standing limit for this landlord is on file, and no quote or cost figure appears anywhere in the case.
The tenant confirmed on 14 Oct that someone would be home for the 20 Oct PM slot; the slot was recorded as 2024-10-20 13:00.
The provider missed the confirmed 20 Oct appointment; the case was held and the visit moved to the following day group, with the work reported done on 24 Oct.
The provider reported the job complete on 24 Oct: a new Fluidmaster bottom-entry ball valve supplied and installed to the WC, with the basin taps reported fine by the tenants.
The landlord pays the contractor directly and the request was marked completed without payment through the agency.
No management key was issued for the visit: the tenant stated someone would be home, which contradicts the boilerplate access line in the agency's own confirmation email.
A contractor called the tenant on 15 Nov 2024, three weeks after completion; the transcript records only the greeting, so the purpose is unknown.

conflicts.description: Agency records disagree on which firm holds the job: Riverside Works is named in the email to the landlord and in the work-order brief; Willow Services is named in the tenant brief, every chaser and every booking confirmation. Three different contact numbers appear for the same job (07700 900781, 07700 900552, 07700 900511).

conflicts.resolution: The tenant's own reply settles a tenant-owned fact (RTE-TENANT) and a specific statement beats boilerplate: no key was issued, so key return does not arise.

conflicts.resolution: Tenant asked to confirm both the WC fill and the basin tap before closure (ACT-2); the job will be reopened with the provider if the tap is still faulty.
